top3.headline: Cursor ships live apps that leave localhost
top3.whyItMatters: Cloud agents now scaffold, secure-check, and publish shareable tools on every paid plan.

top3.headline: Claude Code put user email in web User-Agent
top3.whyItMatters: A default privacy plugin now blocks the leak; agent harnesses can expose identity without asking.

top3.headline: Perplexity runs 10k internal work agents
top3.whyItMatters: Teammates already outnumber staff twenty to one; headcount planning just changed for Max users.

items.title: Naval: hard-to-build tech is where progress starts
items.takeaway: Naval argues progress comes from hard-to-build technology born in competitive free-market capitalism in one precarious place, then diffuses; snuffing that out means long global stagnation.
items.soWhat: Leaders betting on frontier tech are also betting on the fragile ecosystems that still invent it.

items.title: Claude Code sent user email in User-Agent headers
items.takeaway: GitHub issue #107757 and HN (201) report Claude Code put the user's email in User-Agent on web searches; Anthropic's cc-plugin-privacy in v2.1.317+ blocks it by default.
items.soWhat: Audit what your coding agent sends outbound; identity leaks can ride inside routine tool calls.

items.title: Lyn Alden: air-gapped critical systems still make sense
items.takeaway: Lyn Alden, citing FAA experience and AI-era hacking, argues nuclear, air-traffic, and core bank systems on offline rarely updated media can be sound design, not folly.
items.soWhat: For existential systems, slow updates and isolation can beat always-online innovation.

image.alt: @LynAldenContact on X: Lyn Alden: air-gapped critical systems still make sense

items.title: Meta Muse adds two-way voice and expressive avatar
items.takeaway: The Verge reports Meta's Muse AI now has a two-way voice mode with a more expressive avatar, extending Muse beyond text chat.
items.soWhat: Personal agents are becoming multimodal interfaces, not just chat boxes.

items.title: Cursor lets cloud agents build and publish live apps
items.takeaway: Build Live Apps scaffolds a web app, provisions Postgres and Cursor-SSO auth, runs security checks, and returns a shareable link; available on all paid plans with cloud agents.
items.soWhat: Internal tools can leave localhost with one publish step under admin review.

items.title: Hermes Agent v0.23 Hearth unifies every chat surface
items.takeaway: Nous Research ships Desktop-in-browser, one gateway for CLI/TUI/Desktop/bots/cron, /Rewind, group-chat routing, and spend limits on paid MCP tools after ~10k commits.
items.soWhat: Open agent stacks are consolidating sessions and spend controls into one local gateway.

items.title: LangChain ships async subagents for Deep Agents
items.takeaway: Orchestrators stay responsive while background subagents run long work; start/check/update/cancel/list tools plus interrupt vs enqueue steering land in Python, JS, and Managed Deep Agents.
items.soWhat: Agent products that block on every tool call will feel broken next to async peers.

items.title: Claude Personal Finance connects banks via Plaid
items.takeaway: US beta on Pro/Max/Ultra lets users link accounts read-only for up to two years of transactions; Claude cannot move funds or give investment advice, and chats are not used for training.
items.soWhat: Money Q&A moves into the assistant; leaders should decide what finance data agents may see.

items.title: Perplexity Teammates: always-on work agents on Max
items.takeaway: Teammates use Computer projects/skills/memory, collaborate, and message Slack; Max web preview today. CEO Aravind Srinivas says ~10,000 ran internally in 30 days (~20× headcount).
items.soWhat: Workforce planning now includes agent headcount, not just human seats.

voices.quote: Actual progress comes from hard-to-build technology. Which comes from competitive, creative, free-market capitalism. Which comes from one small, precarious area.
We have about 10,000 teammates (within the last 30 days) in Perplexity's internal workspace right now. That's already 20x our headcount.
Having nuclear codes, air traffic systems, and core bank systems on offline floppy drives that never updated is not the worst thing, given the increasing era of hacking.
most of the agents we're building inside langchain leverage async subagents in a meaningful way
You can now build live apps in Cursor and share them with a link. Agents have made it easier to write code, but most apps never make it off localhost.
